data: The first celestial body whose orbit was deliberately altered by humans. NASA's DART struck Dimorphos at 6.14 km/s on 2022-09-26, shortening its 11.9-hour orbit around Didymos by 33 minutes (4.2%) — exceeding the success threshold by ~25× and demonstrating planetary defense is possible.

160-m moonlet orbiting Didymos at 1.2 km separation. Impact target of NASA's DART on 2022-09-26 — first demonstration of kinetic-impactor planetary defense. DART's 6.14 km/s impact shortened Dimorphos's orbital period around Didymos by 33 minutes (4.2%), exceeding the 73-second success threshold by ~25×. The surface turned out to be 'rubble-pile fluid' — DART sank ~50 cm into the surface during the half-second of contact.
DART — NASA, 26 September 2022 (kinetic impactor; first deliberate asteroid orbit change)
Dimorphos orbits Didymos at a mere 1.2 km — and after DART, its orbital period changed by 33 minutes. The first deliberate orbit change of a celestial body by humans.
The two extreme points on every elliptical orbit: closest approach, and farthest.
